sources.body: <p>La izquierda salió este jueves a la ofensiva contra el PP y Vox, aprovechando el <a href="https://elpais.com/espana/elecciones-generales/2026-11-26/vox-propone-un-recorte-del-gasto-publico-de-las-dimensiones-de-la-motosierra-de-milei.html" target="_self" rel="" title="https://elpais.com/espana/elecciones-generales/2026-11-26/vox-propone-un-recorte-del-gasto-publico-de-las-dimensiones-de-la-motosierra-de-milei.html">masivo plan de recortes</a> anunciado por la ultraderecha y la falta de condena de Santiago Abascal a la violencia de género. En un debate vivo, tenso, duro, en el que Alberto Núñez Feijóo anunció que dimitirá si no es presidente, Pedro Sánchez mejoró su desempeño con respecto al jueves pasado. Fue con la ayuda de <a href="https://elpais.com/espana/elecciones-generales/2026-11-19/ada-colau-la-ultraderecha-ha-sabido-diagnosticar-mejor-que-el-psoe-el-malestar-de-la-ciudadania.html" target="_self" rel="" title="https://elpais.com/espana/elecciones-generales/2026-11-19/ada-colau-la-ultraderecha-ha-sabido-diagnosticar-mejor-que-el-psoe-el-malestar-de-la-ciudadania.html">Ada Colau</a>. La candidata de Frente Amplio <a href="https://elpais.com/espana/elecciones-generales/2026-11-26/quien-ha-ganado-el-debate-los-analistas-de-el-pais-se-decantan-por-ada-colau.html" target="_self" rel="" title="https://elpais.com/espana/elecciones-generales/2026-11-26/quien-ha-ganado-el-debate-los-analistas-de-el-pais-se-decantan-por-ada-colau.html">destacó</a>, viva y con iniciativa, interpelando a todos, dictando el guion, recordando el <a href="https://elpais.com/espana/elecciones-generales/2023-07-20/yolanda-diaz-usa-el-debate-para-apelar-a-la-victoria-el-23-j-vamos-a-ganar-las-elecciones-como-ganamos-ayer.html" target="_self" rel="" title="https://elpais.com/espana/elecciones-generales/2023-07-20/yolanda-diaz-usa-el-debate-para-apelar-a-la-victoria-el-23-j-vamos-a-ganar-las-elecciones-como-ganamos-ayer.html">buen papel de Yolanda Díaz en el debate a tres de 2023</a>. “¡Ada, remontada!”, le cantaban los suyos tras terminar. Las dos fuerzas de la izquierda parecieron más complementarias que las de derechas, que prácticamente se ignoraron. Feijóo, a diferencia de la semana pasada, no fue el dominador de la escena y acabó —ya tras el debate— retirando a medias <a href="https://elpais.com/espana/elecciones-generales/2026-11-26/colau-cuestiona-a-feijoo-que-mantenga-a-mazon-aforado-y-el-lider-del-pp-le-contesta-que-estuvo-calladita.html" target="_self" rel="" title="https://elpais.com/espana/elecciones-generales/2026-11-26/colau-cuestiona-a-feijoo-que-mantenga-a-mazon-aforado-y-el-lider-del-pp-le-contesta-que-estuvo-calladita.html">unas palabras por las que estaba siendo acusado de machista</a>.</p><p><a href="https://elpais.com/espana/elecciones-generales/2026-11-26/la-izquierda-sale-a-la-ofensiva-contra-abascal-y-feijoo-por-los-recortes-y-la-violencia-de-genero.html" target="_blank">Seguir leyendo</a></p>
sources.headline: La izquierda sale a la ofensiva contra Abascal y Feijóo por los recortes y la violencia machista

sources.body:
Penúltim dia de campanya per a les eleccions del 29N, marcat per l' únic debat a quatre de la campanya , que ha enfrontat Pedro Sánchez, Alberto Núñez Feijóo, Santiago Abascal i Ada Colau.

Els principals candidats a la presidència del govern espanyol han contraposat propostes en un debat organitzat per l'Acadèmia de la Televisió, una batalla dialèctica que ha arrencat amb els retrets per l' habitatge.

Colau ha suspès el govern de Pedro Sánchez en aquesta matèria i ha exigit mesures "valentes" per reeditar el govern de coalició , com expropiar pisos a fons voltor i abaixar els lloguers un 30%. No ha recollit el guant el candidat del PSOE, que s'ha compromès a construir més pisos i "esquivar" el bloqueig de les comunitats del PP a la llei d'Habitatge.

La candidata de Front Ampli ha alertat dels retrocessos amb un possible govern de PP i Vox . Colau i Sánchez han atacat Feijóo per un possible pacte amb el candidat de Vox, l'únic que no ha condemnat la violència masclista.

Al seu lloc, Abascal ha vinculat delinqüència amb immigració i ha acusat l'executiu d'haver "importat" violadors, i ha focalitzat les crítiques en Sánchez, a qui ha culpat del "veritable retrocés" dels últims vuit anys, després d'enumerar els accidents de tren, la corrupció, l'apagada i la "immigració massiva".

Feijóo ha lamentat que els ciutadans no arriben a final de mes. Arran d'aquestes paraules, la candidata de Front Ampli li ha preguntat per què han votat tants cops contra la pujada del salari mínim , i Feijóo ha acabat dient que estava d'acord amb l'increment.

Al seu torn, el president espanyol ha acusat els líders de PP i Vox de "disfressar-se de Robin Hood" fent creure que "defensen els més necessitats quan voten contra les mesures que els beneficien", com la revalorització de les pensions amb l'IPC o els topalls dels lloguers.

PP i Vox han coincidit en la proposta d'abaixar impostos i Sánchez ha acusat els d'Abascal de proposar una retallada "amb la motoserra" , una retallada que Colau ha assegurat que és "11 cops més gran" que la que va aplicar Mariano Rajoy i molt similar a la de Milei a l'Argentina, que ha caigut en recessió.

Feijóo ha tornat a prometre una "auditoria de dalt a baix" si arriba a La Moncloa, per destapar el "saqueig al pressupost dels espanyols", unes acusacions de corrupció a les quals Sánchez ha assegurat que ha actuat amb "tolerància zero" i Colau ha reivindicat que la "corrupció zero sí que existeix", i ha posat com a exemple el seu pas a l'alcaldia de Barcelona.

Com ja va passar en el cara a cara de fa una setmana, Feijóo ha preguntat a Sánchez per les donacions de les primàries que el van portar al capdavant del PSOE: "Expliqui la trama i deixi de tapar la corrupció", li ha dit. L'actual president espanyol ha respost que les van finançar militants socialistes.

En un debat amb reiterades enganxades entre els candidats i en què Sánchez ha passat més a l'ofensiva que en el cara a cara, el candidat socialista ha plantejat a Feijóo si reconeixerà els resultats del 29N en cas d'una victòria del PSOE. "Sí o no? No ho diu", li ha etzibat.
sources.headline: La corrupció, l'habitatge i les acusacions de masclisme tensionen el debat a 4 per al 29N

Imagen de la jura de bandera de Sánchez durante la mili. La foto fue distribuida por el equipo del candidato tras el debate

“El usted calladita” de Alberto Núñez Feijóo dirigido a Ada Colau ha quedado como la frase que quedará en la memoria colectiva del debate a cuatro entre los candidatos a la Presidencia del Gobierno, Pedro Sánchez (PSOE), Alberto Núñez Feijóo (PP), Santiago Abascal (Vox) y Ada Colau (Frente Amplio) de las elecciones generales del 29 de noviembre del 2026. Pero el debate, en el que la candidata del Frente Amplio y el líder del PSOE han hecho pinza sobre el líder de la oposición mientras el de Vox mostraba su discurso más duro, ha dado otros momentos significativos. Colau se ha solidarizado con la esposa del presidente, Feijóo ha anunciado que dimitirá si no gobierna, Abascal se ha negado a condenar la violencia de género y Sánchez ha presumido de ser el único en haber hecho la mili y haber jurado la bandera.

A continuación presentamos las frases más destacadas del debate distribuidas por los bloques tratados: Vivienda; Economía y Fiscalidad; Política Social y Servicios Públicos; Lucha contra la corrupción y regeneración democrática; Migración y política exterior.

stories.headline: European leaders choose Pablo Hernández de Cos to succeed Christine Lagarde at the ECB

sources.body:
Former Bank of Spain governor chosen to succeed Christine Lagarde after winning support of EU’s biggest countries

Spain’s Pablo Hernández de Cos has been chosen as the next president of the European Central Bank , to succeed Christine Lagarde, after winning support from the EU’s biggest countries.

The economist and monetary policymaker will become the first Spaniard to lead the ECB, defeating his rival candidate Klaas Knot, the former head of the Dutch central bank.

EU diplomats agreed two other appointments to the ECB’s executive board on Thursday: France’s Laurence Boone and Germany’s Markus Brunnermeier. The trio of appointments was a package deal, after France and Germany converged on choosing Hernández de Cos, who is expected to keep the ECB on the same path.

Following the talks European Council president António Costa confirmed the three appointments, saying: “This will pave the way for the formal appointment of the new ECB leadership by the EUCO [European Council] in December.”

The French president, Emmanuel Macron, also confirmed: “A consensus emerged on the nominations to the European Central Bank.”

The Spanish prime minister, Pedro Sánchez, who faces elections this weekend that he is predicted to lose, celebrated the victory of Hernández de Cos and the presence of Spaniards in other big EU roles, by hailing “a Spain that is leading in Europe as never before”.

Spain’s former deputy prime minister Teresa Ribera is one of the European Commission’s executive vice-presidents, with responsibility for a vast portfolio spanning the green transition and EU competition policy. The former Spanish economy minister Nadia Calviño leads the European Investment Bank.

Hernández de Cos, a former Bank of Spain governor, will become the fifth head of the eurozone’s central bank since it was founded in 1998. He is expected to take up his position after Lagarde stands down in February, during a time of political change and economic pressure in the 21-country eurozone.

Europe is entering a big election year, starting with Spain’s elections this weekend, with national votes to follow in France, Italy and (non-eurozone) Poland. European economies are under growing pressure from fierce Chinese competition, US tariff threats and soaring energy prices that are driving up inflation, as well as high debt in several member states.

One of his biggest challenges will be reining in surging prices: inflation in the eurozone hit 4% last month, up from 2.1% a year earlier.

Hernández de Cos, who is now serving as general manager of the Bank for International Settlements, is seen as supporting lower interest rates to boost growth.

Market analysts are closely watching what Hernández de Cos might say about France, where an embattled minority government is struggling to pass a budget. French debt is forecast to hit 122% of GDP next year, more than twice the limit allowed under EU fiscal rules.

Arne Petimezas, the director of research at AFS Group Amsterdam, said Hernández de Cos, who “leans dovish”, was the “continuity candidate”. He added: “Don’t expect de Cos to turn a blind eye to France and its fiscal predicaments. No carte blanche: bond buying will remain contingent on austerity and a path towards a lower debt ratio.”
sources.headline: Spain’s Pablo Hernández de Cos wins race to be next ECB president

sources.body: Spanish monetary economist Pablo Hernandez de Cos on Thursday was set to replace France's Christine Lagarde as the new head of the European Central Bank (ECB). His nomination comes as the Europe's most powerful financial institution grapples with an Iran war-driven resurgence in inflation and a cost of living crisis.
sources.headline: Spanish economist de Cos to succeed Lagarde as head of ECB

stories.headline: Two Italians are killed in a strike on Kuwait and Iran denies responsibility

sources.body:
Two Italian nationals have died following a strike on a facility in Kuwait which both countries have blamed on Iran.

The pair were technicians working for German arms manufacturing company Rheinmetall, Italy's foreign ministry said.

Iran has denied responsibility for the attack, with Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi saying the incident looked "suspicious" and that Tehran would work with Kuwait and Italy to "determine the cause".

Kuwait's defence ministry said earlier that four people - the two Italians, a Kuwaiti national and Pakistani national - had been injured from falling shrapnel after a number of drones from Iran were detected and intercepted.

It comes just over a week after Kuwait said it had repelled overnight Iranian drone attacks on an airbase which hosts US forces - the first strikes in more than two months on the country.

Recent exchanges of fire between the US and Iran, and a deadlock in negotiations, have raised fears of a major escalation in the war.

The conflict began when US and Israel attacked Iran in late February, with Iran retaliating by launching missiles and drones at Israel and Gulf Arab states hosting US military assets and personnel.

On Thursday, Araghchi said he had expressed condolences over the deaths in calls with his Italian and Kuwaiti counterparts and that the incident looked like a "precooked recipe for war", without expanding further.

Earlier, the country's armed forces spokesperson Abolfazl Shekarchi said "no military or offensive operations have been conducted" by Iran.

Kuwait's Army said the latest attack was on a "vital site in the country" and was the result of "heinous Iranian aggression", while confirming the deaths of the two Italian nationals.

Italy's foreign minister was quoted by Italian media as saying that investigations showed that the drone used in the attack was manufactured in Iran and that Iranian proxies were known to carry out attacks in the region.

"The Rheinmetall Group is in deep mourning," the German firm said in a statement confirming the deaths of two of its staff members.

"Two highly valued employees lost their lives while carrying out their professional duties, as they were providing technical support for air defence systems," it added.

"Protecting people in the country was a matter of profound importance to them.

"Company management and the workforce are devastated that our colleagues have now lost their lives."

Italian media outlets have named the two individuals. One of the men was reported to be 36, while the other was 65 and nearing retirement.

The men had been performing maintenance on systems used by the Kuwait Armed Forces, according to Italian press agency Ansa citing Italy's foreign ministry.

Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni wrote on X: "On my own behalf and on behalf of the government, I express my deepest sympathy and offer my heartfelt condolences to the victims' families.

"My thoughts are with all those affected by the attack and their families."

European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen wrote on social media: "We must step up pressure on Iran to end these unacceptable attacks against its neighbours and our partners in the Gulf.
sources.headline: Two Italians killed in strike in Kuwait, as Iran denies responsibility

stories.headline: Zelensky warns of a major Russian attack and calls for more US pressure on Moscow

sources.body:
Trump says he urged Putin to ‘pull back’ military aggression in Europe amid escalating Russian and Ukrainian attacks.

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy says Ukraine has information that Russia is preparing a new mass strike on the country in the coming days.

“Unfortunately, we have information about a new mass strike being prepared by the Russians,” he said in his nightly video address on Thursday. “In the coming days, please pay attention to the alarms of missile threats.”

It was the second such warning from Zelenskyy this week. He also had a message for Moscow: “We will rebuild what is ours and retaliate against every Russian strike.”

US President Donald Trump said he had pressed Russian President Vladimir Putin to ease Russia’s military actions in Europe.

In a post on Truth Social, Trump said he spent “a lot of time” in talks with Putin in China on the issue of Putin pulling back “all Military aggression against territories throughout Europe”.

“Thousands of people are being killed each and every month, A COMPLETE BLOODBATH,” Trump wrote. He said he hoped that would allow a deal between Russia and Ukraine to be “made quickly”, which he called “a strong possibility”.

Trump said he updated NATO Secretary-General Mark Rutte on the talks during a meeting at his Mar-a-Lago club in Florida on Wednesday night.

Russia struck Kyiv with ballistic missiles overnight, wounding seven people and hitting a shopping centre and two other buildings, Mayor Vitali Klitschko said.

Moscow said it hit drone-related sites in the city. Russian forces have attacked Kyiv and other cities almost continuously since September.

Ukraine said its drones hit an oil refinery in Russia’s southern Krasnodar region, oil reservoirs at a Transneft facility in Bashkortostan and the Marinovka military airfield in the Volgograd region.

Ukraine has also widened its attacks at sea. On Monday, Zelenskyy said Ukraine used seven naval drones to hit the Russian corvette Merkury and the cargo ship Angara off Libya . Libyan officials told the Associated Press news agency that the Merkury was heavily damaged but not sunk.

At about the same time, a suspected Ukrainian drone struck the Russia-bound cargo ship Sparta II in the Baltic Sea, near Finland. Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov called the attacks a “ very dangerous trend “.

At least four Russian vessels have been targeted this month.

European Union leaders are struggling at a summit in Brussels to agree on a new 45 billion euro ($49bn) loan to help Ukraine meet its economic and military needs next year. It would come on top of a 90 billion euro ($99bn) loan , agreed nearly a year ago, that covers most of Ukraine’s government needs for 2026 and 2027.

Early on Friday in Brussels, European Council President Antonio Costa said that 24 member states supported the new loan , as talks on the bloc’s next seven-year budget stretched on.

The loan is tangled up with the EU’s budget for 2028 to 2034, which includes about $110bn for Ukraine over seven years. German Chancellor Friedrich Merz has threatened to hold up the budget unless all member states make a “collective commitment” to Ukraine.
sources.headline: 3 , Zelenskyy warns of major Russian attack as Trump urges Putin to ‘pull back’

sources.body:
Volodymyr Zelensky has voiced deep frustration with the US, saying delays in delivering vital anti-ballistic missiles are costing Ukrainian lives and complaining that the US is not pushing Russia hard enough in peace talks.

In an interview with the BBC at his central Kyiv office, Ukraine's president also said it was "strange" that Donald Trump had posted a photo of himself embracing Vladimir Putin as "my friend".

"Of course it's up to the President of the United States, but... it's strange," Zelensky said, speaking in English.

"He's an aggressor, and a killer…He can't be a friend. Just cannot be," he said, adding it was like saying you were friends with Adolf Hitler during World War Two.

Since a bruising encounter with Trump in the Oval Office in 2025, Zelensky has been careful how he handles relations with the United States.

Trump's two envoys have been trying to negotiate a peace deal between Russia and Ukraine - to end the huge loss of life. But they often seem more in tune with Moscow's position, than that of Kyiv.

The latest round of peace talks, mediated in Abu Dhabi earlier this month, made no obvious progress: "The more we know, the more problems", is how Zelensky described it.

He said talks were expected to resume in December.

On Thursday, Donald Trump posted on his Truth Social platform that at his own summit with Putin in China last week he had urged Russia to "pull back all military aggression against territories throughout Europe" and said he believed a peace deal with Ukraine was "a strong possibility".

But from its public statements, Russia appears to have regressed to its initial, hardline negotiating positions – on everything.

And Zelensky revealed that it was not clear whether European negotiators would be at the table, as the US envoys had announced .

Ukraine urgently needs the talks to move forward and bring five exhausting years of Russia's full-scale invasion to an end.

Russian strikes across the country have been growing more frequent and more deadly: the number of civilians being killed is at an all-time high.

So Zelensky called for "real helpful allies, who can push Russia" to achieve results and urged the US to live up to its reputation as a strong country with "power and respect".

"When you try to be very neutral with the aggressor... it means you support victims and you support also aggressor. It's not right," he said.

The US argues that it is neutral: in the complex search for a peace deal between the two sides that can hold.

In the meantime, Kyiv is struggling to defend its skies.

The air alerts, day and night, are now a draining feature of everyday life. As Russian ballistic missiles target power stations and bridges, jet-powered drones are launched daily at central Kyiv and other big cities.

Ukraine launches hundreds of drones at targets in Russia in response.

Zelensky said the military here are now able to destroy about 70% of Russia's fastest drones, a statistic he said was improving.

But there is a "very, very big" deficit of interceptors to stop ballistic missiles and he said the Amercians were delaying deliveries of its Patriot systems.
sources.headline: US too focused on Middle East and not pushing Russia hard enough, Zelensky tells BBC

sources.body: US President Donald Trump said Thursday he had asked Vladimir Putin to "pull back all military aggression" against Europe, in a shift in tone towards the leader Russian he called his friend just a week ago. Trump said he had made the request to Putin when they met in China last week, adding that he thought it would help lead to a deal to end Moscow's grinding war in Ukraine. The US leader's comments come a day after he hosted NATO chief Mark Rutte in Florida, after which they issued a joint statement calling on Russia not to expand the Ukraine war. FRANCE 24's international affairs editor Kethevane Gorjestani explains.
sources.headline: Trump urges Putin to end 'military aggression' in Europe

sources.body: Five Israeli strikes and a shooting overnight and on Thursday killed 10 Palestinians across Gaza, according to officials at Shifa and Al-Aqsa Martyrs hospitals, where the casualties were taken. A strike on a residential apartment in Deir Al-Balah in central Gaza killed a man and his wife, the officials said. FRANCE 24's Jennie Shin speaks with journalist Ahmed Dremly, who was in Gaza until six months ago and has extensively covered the humanitarian crisis there.

stories.headline: New Zealand’s governing coalition falls one seat short of a majority in the final count

sources.body:
New Zealand's ruling coalition has fallen short of a parliamentary majority by one seat, following a campaign shaped by a sluggish economy and disillusioned voters.

It now needs the support of the centrist Opportunity Party to remain in power. If they cannot reach a deal, the country may have to go back to the polls.

The incumbent National Party led by Prime Minister Christopher Luxon secured 40 out of 130 seats, while its coalition partners ACT and New Zealand First took 13 and 12 respectively.

A government led by the centre-left Labour Party is not possible, official results on Friday show, as the bloc would not have enough seats even if Opportunity threw its weight behind it.

Luxon on Friday acknowledged that negotiations "may be challenging" and will take some time.

"Kiwis won't thank us for rushing to an agreement that falls apart or for sending them back to the polls," he told reporters.

Labour leader Chris Hipkins said his party "ran an incredible campaign" but acknowledged that it doesn't have negotiating power despite winning the popular vote. "More New Zealanders voted for change at this election than for the status quo," he said.

New Zealand's mixed-member proportional voting system means most governments are coalitions. Each person casts two votes – one for their preferred political party and another for their choice of local representative.

Labour secured 36 seats, The Greens took 17, while Te Pāti Māori, which represents Māori interests, picked up five.

Opportunity, which has been described as this election's kingmaker, secured seven seats. Opportunity's leader Qiulae Wong told reporters her party will negotiate with National, but that all options remain on the table.

"There are seven parties in parliment and everyone is responsible for making sure we do everything we can to deliver a stable government for New Zealand. It's not just up to us," she said on Friday.

Preliminary results on 7 November, election day, had projected that National combined with its coalition partners would have a slim lead over the left-leaning bloc.

But today's official tally shows it had lost two seats on special votes - cast by citizens who were overseas or outside of their registered electorate on election day - which typically skew left.

Some of National's key election pledges include lower taxes, cheaper energy, more renewable generation, and a greater focus on defence.

Labour, meanwhile, had campaigned to cut healthcare, public transport and fuel costs, more government support for social housing, among other things.

In earlier interviews with the BBC, many voters had expressed frustration over spiralling costs of living and high unemployment across the country, with declining faith in their political leadership.

"There's this kind of apathy and a bit of dread," said 21-year-old Imogen Vlutger.

A 40-year-old man said he didn't vote as he could not bring himself to tick any of the boxes on the ballot paper.

More than half of the country no longer see New Zealand as a land of opportunity, according to a survey by the Helen Clark Foundation, a public policy think tank.
sources.headline: New Zealand's ruling coalition falls short of parliamentary majority by one seat

sources.body:
Incumbent prime minister Christopher Luxon loses majority and needs support of Opportunity party to remain in power, or country faces another election

The final results of New Zealand’s general election show the incumbent rightwing coalition will need the support of a centrist newcomer party to form a government, and to avoid sending the country back to the polls.

Preliminary results on 7 November handed the National party and its two coalition partners, the populist New Zealand First and libertarian Act parties, a slim two-seat majority, making the election too close to call until final votes were tallied.

On Friday, the electoral commission released the results from nearly 485,000 “special votes” – those cast from overseas or outside a voter’s electorate. National dropped two seats to 40, Labour stayed on 36 seats, the Greens picked up one seat to 17, Act had 13, New Zealand First 12, Opportunity seven and Te Pati Māori five.

The National-led bloc currently has 65 seats. In the 130-seat parliament, 66 seats are needed for a majority.

The revised results mean the National-led coalition has the only realistic path to power – if it can negotiate a deal with Opportunity. If it cannot, New Zealand will probably need to hold another election.

Three electorate seats changed hands after the special votes. Labour won Wairarapa off National with just 81 votes, and took Hamilton East from National with 173 votes. The Greens won Wellington Bays from Labour with 1,610 votes.

If National applies for a recount and wins back just one of those seats, it could return to power with a slim majority and without needing Opportunity. Applications for a recount must be made by 3 December, and results could take another five days.

Special votes in previous elections have favoured the left, and typically have cost the right one or two seats. Until Friday, a question mark hung over whether National would be able to govern comfortably alongside its coalition partners, or whether it would be forced to cut a deal with the Opportunity party – a newcomer centrist party that incumbent prime minister Christopher Luxon had previously ruled out working with.

After the election, Luxon softened his stance on his initial rule-out, saying he intended to find common ground with the Opportunity party.

On Friday afternoon, Luxon said National will now begin formal negotiations with New Zealand First, Act and Opportunity, but he cautioned discussions would be “challenging” and could take some time.

“Getting it right matters far more than getting it done quickly,” Luxon said. “Kiwis won’t thank us for rushing to an agreement that falls apart, or for sending them back to the polls.”

Lara Greaves, a political scientist at Victoria University of Wellington, said the prospect of New Zealand heading back to the polls was unprecedented, because negotiations between the four parties will be so complex.

“It’s not a 0% chance, it’s the highest chance we’ve ever had of it being another election,” she said.

Opportunity, led by Auckland businesswoman Qiulae Wong , has long said it will negotiate first with the party that secures the highest number of seats.
sources.headline: New Zealand election: final results show ruling coalition needs minor party to govern

stories.headline: UK net migration falls to its lowest level since 1997

sources.body:
Net migration to the UK has fallen to 77,000 in the year to the end of June - the lowest level this century, other than during the pandemic, Office for National Statistics (ONS) figures show.

Excluding the limited movements of people during the worldwide travel restrictions in 2020, the figures show the number of people arriving in the UK, minus those leaving, tumbled 92% from the record high of 944,000 in the year to March 2023.

The ONS said this was the lowest net migration since 1997.

Net migration is a measure of how many extra people are added to the population in a given year.

Prime Minister Andy Burnham said the figures showed there was now "a sufficient degree of control" over the migration system.

The prime minister went on to say: "I'm not going to say all of the work is done, and I don't want to appear complacent, but I think we're finally as a country getting into the position that the public has long wanted to see."

The underlying official statistics show that an estimated 738,000 people immigrated to the UK in the year to June while 661,000 emigrated.

Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood said the figures showed that Labour had "delivered" after Conservative failures - but Chris Philp, her Tory shadow, said restrictions introduced by his party before the 2024 General Election were behind the falls.

The 77,000 figure is also the first time the UK has seen net migration in the tens of thousands since former PM David Cameron's controversial pledge 16 years ago to reach such a level.

The biggest factors in Thursday's record low were falls in the arrivals of people coming from outside Europe in three major categories of migration: The number of people coming to the UK to work fell by 45,000, asylum claims fell by 19,000 and the total number of students fell by 33,000.

These number had been expected to fall because of the tightening of visas rules that began under the previous Conservative government which was then continued by Labour from July 2024.

The effect of those policies, plus emigration from the UK, has meant that while net migration had already begun to fall, it more than halved in the last 12 months alone.

Mahmood said the figures showed the government had "restored control".

"We have brought net migration to 77,000, down 92% from its peak under the Conservatives," she said. "Where they failed, we have delivered for the British people."

This is a reference to the so-called "Boriswave" after Brexit. When the UK left the EU and its freedom of movement rules, Boris Johnson's government allowed in many more people to work and study from other parts of the world.

That led to the record-breaking arrivals in the year to March 2023. Johnson's successor, Rishi Sunak, introduced major restrictions on visas in the last months of his government.

Shadow home secretary Chris Philp said the falls were a result of those changes.

In a post on X, he called for an "annual legally binding inward migration cap, set by Parliament, at far lower levels".

Dr Ben Brindle of Oxford University's Migration Observatory, an impartial expert body, said: "We are entering an unusual period where immigration has come down and may still have further to fall - but we still have relatively high emigration, at least for the time being.
sources.headline: UK net migration at lowest level since 1997 as asylum claims also fall

sources.body:
Labour is jubilant it has got numbers down to levels the Tories could not but it was helped by factors beyond its control

Net migration to UK falls to lowest level since 1997 excluding pandemic

David Cameron was the leader of the opposition when he made a comment on overall migration that was used to interrogate every Tory leader for the next 14 years.

Asked in January 2010 on the BBC by the interviewer Andrew Marr to address comments made by the archbishop of Canterbury calling for the population to remain under 70 million, Cameron said net immigration levels of 200,000 a year were “too much”.

“We would like to see net immigration in the tens of thousands rather than the hundreds of thousands,” he said.

It became a full-blown promise in Cameron’s Tory manifesto that year; and it was there again when he won the 2015 general election, alongside a promise to hold an EU referendum. And the promise was repeated by Theresa May in 2017 as she narrowly defeated the then Labour leader, Jeremy Corbyn.

Both Tory leaders struggled with the actual net migration numbers, which fluctuated between 195,000 and 303,000.

Boris Johnson was pressed on whether he would revive Cameron’s pledge, and his 2019 manifesto said “overall numbers will come down”. Rishi Sunak, five years later, said he would like to see the figures get to tens of thousands but his manifesto promised that “numbers would fall every year”.

It has led to some crowing by Labour – and frustration from the Tories – that numbers have finally dipped below six figures under the current government.

Migration analysts said the Tories struggled throughout the 2010s because the UK was a full member of the EU and had no way of controlling inward EU migration.

EU citizens made up a majority of immigration and net migration in the run-up to the 2016 EU referendum. Since 2022, however, EU net migration has been negative.

As the UK emerged from the Covid pandemic, Johnson opened the doors to non-EU migration and to Ukrainians and people from Hong Kong.

Madeleine Sumption, the director of the Migration Observatory at the University of Oxford, said: “The previous government introduced some relatively liberal policies, including visa schemes for care workers, mid-skilled workers, Ukrainians and Hongkongers, and post-study work visas for international students.”

Several conditions that enabled Labour to achieve net migration of below 100,000 did not exist for most of the time that the Tories were in power, Sumption said.

First, the UK was part of the EU for most of the Tories’ time in office and so it had little control over inward EU migration.

Second, the Office for National Statistics still relied on an older methodology for estimating migration of British citizens under the Conservatives . The new method, introduced last year, has taken “tens of thousands off the net migration figure”, she said.

Sign up for the Breaking News UK email to get newsletter alerts direct to your inbox

Third, high migration under the previous government – and particularly under Johnson – has left a temporary legacy of high numbers of non-EU citizens leaving the UK under Labour.
sources.headline: How much of the sharp fall in UK immigration is due to Labour’s policies?

stories.headline: Thanksgiving storms leave nearly a million without power and disrupt Maryland’s water supply

sources.body:
Severe weather across the US causes outages and flight delays as families and friends gather for the annual holiday.

Strong winds and heavy storms have knocked out power for nearly a million US homes and businesses and resulted in the rare postponement of Macy’s annual Thanksgiving Day Parade in New York City.

As Americans marked the annual holiday on Thursday, heavy storms disrupted travel across the country, with more than 2,000 flights to or from US destinations delayed and more than 400 cancelled, according to the flight tracking service FlightAware.

More than 900,000 homes and businesses were without electricity on Thursday evening, with the majority in East Coast states, according to the outage tracking website poweroutage.us. New Jersey and parts of New York were placed under a state of emergency.

The US National Weather Service issued wind advisories for northern Georgia, the majority of the mid-Atlantic and southern New England.

Two people were rescued from their cars in New York City due to flooding, according to Mayor Zohran Mamdani.

“There is no destination worth your safety,” Mamdani said. Similar rescues were reported in other coastal communities.

In Maryland, nearly two million water customers in Montgomery and Prince George’s counties were asked to conserve water because of intermittent power disruptions related to heavy rain. The storms also prompted several brief tornado warnings, including for a rare twister southeast of Seattle, Washington.

The Midwestern region witnessed heavy snowfall on Thursday, with some areas of Missouri recording up to 35cm of snow.

Meanwhile, waves driven by high tides caused flooding along the Pacific coast. The conditions were expected to continue into Friday, according to the National Weather Service.

Record tides along the California coast forced evacuations in areas from Humboldt County in the far north to southern Ventura County near Los Angeles.
sources.headline: Thanksgiving storms leave nearly a million without power across the US

sources.body: The Thanksgiving Day request affects nearly 2 million people in Montgomery and Prince George's counties after power issues at two filtration plants.
sources.headline: Maryland residents urged to conserve water after storm disrupts power

sources.body:
A massive Thanksgiving storm hammering the Midwest and north-east with heavy rain and winds, along with high tides out west, is causing widespread disruptions across the US.

More than 80 million Americans expected to be travelling this week. More than 400 flights in the US were cancelled on Thursday and another 2,200 flights into, out of, or within the US were delayed, tracking site FlightAware said.

The FAA has previously warned that delays would be possible "throughout the week" as a result of the rain and wind that are forecast.

Meanwhile, almost one million households were without power on Thursday night, with Pennsylvania, Maryland and Virginia the hardest hit states.

On Thursday, a powerful storm hit the eastern US, bringing damaging winds of up to 70mph, torrential rain, and major coastal flooding.

New Jersey Governor Mikie Sherrill declared a state of emergency as several communities along the Jersey Shore saw widespread flooding.

New York Governor Kathy Hochul also declared a state of emergency for New York City, Long Island and Westchester County.

In New York City, organisers of the annual Macy's Thanksgiving parade have postponed the event to Saturday.

Bridges closed in Maryland due to severe winds and waves battered beaches in Delaware as water seeped onto the boardwalk.

In Maryland, almost two million customers have been asked by the water utility to use water for essential use only due to "intermittent power disruptions".

On the wettest Thanksgiving on record in Washington DC, tidal waters surged and soaked runways at Reagan Washington National Airport, according to the National Water Prediction Service.

More than 980,000 households were reporting power outages by Thursday evening, with Pennsylvania, Virginia, Maryland and New Jersey hit particularly hard.

Pennsylvania Governor Josh Shapiro said that utility providers were working tirelessly to restore power. Meanwhile, energy companies in Virginia and New Jersey warned it may take some time, even days, for power to return, as crews had to wait until it was safe to access damaged areas.

On Thursday afternoon, President Donald Trump said he would consider releasing emergency funds for the east coast as it faces down the holiday storm.

Across the US, severe weather is also descending on the West Coast. The NWS has warned of a series of Pacific storms that are expected to bring rain, mountain snow and strong winds.

Many are bracing for potential flooding as king tides peak along the coast.

Water levels along California's vast coastline could reach over 8ft (2.4 metres) in some areas on Thursday, according to the NWS, breaking records set just last month.

Both San Diego and Los Angeles reported a high tide of over 8ft earlier in the week, and beach-goers were advised to avoid coastal areas.

Train services along the Amtrak Pacific Surfliner, which runs along the California coastline, cancelled several trains due to "washout conditions from high tides", the company shared on social media.

Storms are also forecast for the Pacific Northwest, including the Canadian province of British Columbia.
sources.headline: Major Thanksgiving storm brings flooding, flight delays across US

stories.headline: Diesel tanker capsizes off Ibiza, killing one and prompting checks for a spill

sources.body:
An oil tanker carrying up to 7,000 tonnes of diesel has capsized off the coast of Ibiza, leaving one crew member dead, authorities have said.

The Med Emre, a Malta-flagged vessel, was carrying 17 crew members who were all rescued. However seven were taken to hospital and one was later pronounced dead, Balearic Islands emergency services confirmed.

The six crew receiving treatment reportedly suffered minor injuries, such as hypothermia, Spanish media reports.

The possible environmental damage is being assessed by a plane and Spain's pollution control vessel, Clara Campoamor, which is owned by the country's national maritime rescue service.

"There is still little information available about a possible fuel spill," Balearic Islands' President Marga Prohens wrote on X.

Elena Delgado, maritime captain of Valencia, told news agency AFP that a small slick that had formed around the boat had "disappeared".

"The situation is stabilised," she said, adding that further inspections would be carried out on Friday morning.

Earlier, regional emergencies director Pablo Gárriz said the tanker had not completely sunk, as had originally been reported. The vessel remains partially submerged.

The Med Emre capsized 25 nautical miles (46 km; 29 miles) from Ibiza's coastline and 57 nautical miles from Valencia. It is unclear what caused the sinking.

The chemical tanker was en route from Algeciras, in southern Spain, to Barcelona in the north-east.

Rescuers in Valencia received a distress call around 22:30 local time (21:30 GMT) on Wednesday, according to Spanish media. Minutes later, the vessel reported a leak and the crew said it was leaning at a 90-degree angle.

The injured crew members have been taken to hospitals in Valencia and Can Misses Hospital in Ibiza, President Prohens said.

Ibiza's marine environment was added to the Unesco World Heritage List in 1999. In particular, it is home to dense prairies of Posidonia oceanic seagrass, which is found only in the Mediterranean basin and plays a vital role in supporting local marine biodiversity.

In 2002, Spain experienced one of its worst environmental disasters when the Prestige oil tanker ran into trouble off Galicia's coastline . It spilled more than 60,000 tonnes of heavy fuel oil into the sea.
sources.headline: Diesel tanker carrying up to 7,000 tonnes capsizes near Ibiza, killing one

sources.body:
Así ha quedado el barco naufragado entre València e Ibiza / Delegación del Gobierno

La mancha de contaminación provocada por el hundimiento del buque que transportaba gasoil entre Valencia e Ibiza detectada este jueves al mediodía ha desaparecido y ya no resulta visible. Así lo ha asegurado en su comparecencia de esta tarde la capitana marítima de València, Elena Delgado, que ha atendido a los medios después de recibir el plan preliminar de salvamento por parte del armador del buque. Es un plan, todavía no definitivo, en el que la empresa propone medidas como remolcar el buque a un puerto seguro -se estudiará cuál- y ahora está en proceso de estudio.

Además del documento, la administración realizará una inspección in situ del estado del buque. Tendrá lugar este viernes por la mañana, y en ella se analizará tanto el casco visto como la obra viva, es decir, tanto la parte sumergida como la que no lo está. La llevarán a cabo técnicos de la base logística de salvamento marítimo de Cartagena. Además de expertos en buceo, ha detallado.

Lugar en el que se hundió el buque Med Emre entre València e Ibiza / C. Jover

La capitana también ha dado más información sobre las posibles causas que se barajan para el accidente. En concreto, ha dicho que se ha entrevistado al capitán, que se encuentra en estado de shock y que está a disposición de la autoridad, independiente, de investigación, de accidentes y de la autoridad judicial, a haber habido un fallecimiento como consecuencia del siniestro.

El capitán, ha informado Delgado, habla de un posible ingreso masivo de agua en los tanques del lastre, de una de las bandas del buque, que habría provocado que este se escorara súbitamente sobre una de las bandas. Ha explicado que es habitual que entre agua cuando hay mal tiempo, cosa que ocurrió en este caso, y ha considerado esa posibilidad “una buena noticia en parte”, porque significa que no hay un fallo estructural en los tanques de carga y combustible. Eso explicaría que no hubiera contaminación en el agua, porque los tanques estén intactos.

"Ayer por la noche teníamos cuatro metros de altura de ola en la zona, había muy mal tiempo y el capitán apunta este motivo como la causa de la escora súbita del buque y su posterior vuelco", ha explicado la capitana. Lo que impide normalmente la entrada de agua en ese tipo de barcos es una escotilla que, para que no entre el agua, debería estar cerrada. La investigación determinará si lo estaba esa noche.

“Se han efectuado sobrevuelos sobre el buque y la zona afectada por la contaminación de la que hablábamos esta tarde y ha desaparecido esa mancha, se ha degradado”, ha explicado la capitana. Es decir, que actualmente “no hay contaminación en la zona”.

Por otra parte, el buque de salvamento marítimo Clara Campoamor “ha podido hacer firme un cabo de remolque”. Es decir, que el buque accidentado se encuentra firme a un remolque a este otro barco, lo que lo estabiliza y evita su posible deriva. “Son buenas noticias”, ha dicho.

La Capitanía había hecho un requerimiento al armador para que, en tres horas desde las dos de la tarde, presentara un plan, aunque fuese preliminar, de salvamento del barco, y lo ha hecho. Ahora, ha dicho, ese plan está siendo analizado por las autoridades. Es un documento que incluye medidas de remolque, de inspección y de aseguramiento de la flotación, cálculos de la estiba… en definitiva, una serie “muy detallada” de medidas. Si el análisis concluye que ese plan es suficientemente completo, debería aprobarlo la directora general de la Marina Mercante.
sources.headline: Desaparece la mancha de contaminación del buque volcado entre València e Ibiza y un equipo de buceo inspeccionará el barco mañana

sources.body:
El naufragi del vaixell Med Emre aquesta matinada de dijous a prop d' Eivissa ha posat en alerta els serveis d'emergències i també les entitats ambientalistes, que temen que vessi el gasoil que porta.

Segons ha pogut saber 3CatInfo de fonts properes a l'operatiu de rescat, aquest consistiria a remolcar el vaixell fins al port de Cartagena , l'únic pròxim on pot entrar de manera segura. La previsió és que trigaria uns dos dies a arribar-hi.

Un cop a port s'hauria de posar una barrera al voltant del vaixell per evitar que si hi ha vessaments s'escampin , i començaria l'operació per extreure les 7.000 tones de dièsel que portava d'Algesires a Barcelona.

Les tasques de rescat les hauria de facilitar molt el fet que després del naufragi el vaixell no s'hagi enfonsat , sinó que ha quedat surant i de cap per avall a la superfície del mar. Els 17 tripulants del vaixell els han rescatat, però un d'ells, ferit greu, ha mort a l'hospital.

Segons la Capitania Marítima de València , cap al migdia s'ha detectat una taca de material oliós al voltant del Med Emre, però asseguren que els compartiments de combustible estan " intactes " i que la taca és " mínima ".

La responsable d'aquesta capitania, Elena Delgado , ha dit al vespre que aquesta taca ja havia desaparegut , i que el remolcador de salvament Clara Campoamor ha aconseguit lligar un cable al Med Emre.

D'aquesta manera s'ha estabilitzat el vaixell naufragat i s'evita que vagi a la deriva , a l'espera que es decideix a quin port se'l remolca per extreure'n el combustible que portava.

Delgado ha explicat als periodistes que l'armador del Med Emre ja els ha fet arribar un pla preliminar de salvament , i que aquest divendres bussos i tècnics inspeccionaran el vaixell per saber com està l'estructura.

Un cop es tingui tota aquesta informació, l'armador haurà de completar el pla de salvament, i les autoritats marítimes de les Balears i del País Valencià li donaran el vistiplau o reclamaran canvis.

Delgado ha assegurat que encara no s'ha decidit a quin port es remolcarà el Med Emre, que depèn de l'estat en què estigui el vaixell i que això no se sabrà fins que els tècnics l'hagin inspeccionat.

També ha explicat que el capità del vaixell creu que ha naufragat a causa de " l'entrada massiva d'aigua " als tancs de llast pel mal temps que feia, i que això l'ha desestabilitzat i l'ha fet bolcar.

Segons ha dit, si es confirma aquesta causa, voldrà dir que l'estructura del vaixell està intacta , cosa que hauria de facilitar molt tota l'operació de rescat.

Aquest vaixell, avarat el 2019 a Turquia, té 120 metres de llargada, porta 7.000 tones de gasoil i, s egons Agustí Martín , president de l' Associació Catalana de Capitans de la Marina Mercant , es pot considerar un vaixell de " darrera generació " i, a més, com que té pocs anys, no té els "materials fatigats" per dècades d'ús.

També ha dit que els compartiments interns separats que porta eviten que el combustible es vessi del tot, i que hi ha tècniques i protocols preparats per fer el transvasament, "una operació complexa però que es fa habitualment i és efectiva".
sources.headline: Què passarà amb el gasoil del vaixell naufragat a prop d'Eivissa, que podrien remolcar a Cartagena

stories.headline: More than 163,000 people granted Spanish citizenship under the grandchildren law cannot vote on Sunday

sources.body:
El Tribunal Suprem ha confirmat aquest dijous que finalment els 11.283 nacionalitzats per la llei de nets que ara viuen a Espanya no poden votar el 29N. Quan falten tres dies per a les eleccions generals, el tribunal ha determinat, per tant, que no podran anar a les urnes les més de 163.000 persones nacionalitzades després d'al·legar que eren descendents d'espanyols que van haver d'exiliar-se per la Guerra Civil o represaliats pel franquisme.

La sala ha rebutjat el recurs de l'Advocacia de l'Estat , en nom del govern espanyol, que defensava que la suspensió afectava només el CERA (el cens d'espanyols residents a l'estranger) i, per tant, que els nacionalitzats de la llista que ja vivien o s'havien traslladat a Espanya (inscrits al cens ordinari, el CER) sí que tenien dret a sufragi.

El tribunal, doncs, defensa que " no ha ampliat la mesura cautelar ", sinó que s'ha "limitat a recordar que la suspensió es referia a les persones incloses al llistat facilitat per l'Estat", visquin on visquin.

Segons el tribunal, els magistrats van ordenar a la Junta Electoral Central (JEC) que "cap de les 163.355 persones incloses puguin figurar com electors en el cens, sigui en el d'electors residents absents que viuen a l'estranger o bé al d'electors residents a Espanya".

El tribunal ha precisat, però, que sí que podran votar "les 901 persones que han presentat certificat consular " que ha acreditat que són descendents d'exiliats.

El portaveu del PSOE al Congrés, Patxi López, ha titllat d'"absoluta barbaritat" que el Tribunal Suprem hagi confirmat, a tres dies de les eleccions, que aquestes 163.000 persones nacionalitzades no puguin votar aquest diumenge i se les privi dels "seus drets fonamentals".
sources.headline: Confirmen tres dies abans del 29N que més de 163.000 nacionalitzats amb la llei de nets no podran votar

stories.headline: Barcelona–Madrid high-speed rail fares fall 28% from a year earlier

sources.body:
El prestigi de l'alta velocitat espanyola viu el pitjor moment de la història després dels accidents ferroviaris d'Urda i Adamuz. Totes dues desgràcies van passar a la línia amb destí a Sevilla, però la connexió estrella Barcelona-Madrid també té la desconfiança dels usuaris .

La prova del cotó fluix són els preus. Si hi ha demanda, pugen; si no n'hi ha, baixen. I els preus de l'alta velocitat entre Barcelona i Madrid han caigut un 28% si es compara la primera quinzena de novembre amb el mateix mes de l'any passat.

Segons la monitorització diària de preus que ha fet 3CatInfo entre els dies 30 d'octubre i 15 de novembre, el preu mitjà del bitllet s'ha situat en 62,4 euros respecte a la referència de 86,8 euros del mes complet l'any passat .

Durant els primers dies, els més pròxims a l'accident, els preus van congelar-se o fins i tot caure en alguns casos. Passava un fet inusual: que sortia més barat comprar el bitllet el mateix dia que no pas amb antelació.

La baixa demanda provocada per, o bé usuaris que han deixat de viatjar o bé que han optat per altres transports, com l'avió, el bus o el cotxe, ha fet que els preus ferroviaris –fins i tot els caps de setmana– s'hagin mantingut pràcticament glaçats al llarg de la quinzena, i a uns nivells molt per sota de l'habitual.

Un dels col·lectius que utilitzen més intensivament aquest servei en dona fe. Els directius d'empresa viatgen d'una capital a l'altra amb més freqüència que ningú, moltes vegades anant i tornant el mateix dia o fent breus estades.

El president de l'Associació Espanyola de Directius, Xavier Gangonells, és contundent: "Una part de la gent que agafava el tren ha tornat a l'avió que feia anys que havia deixat enrere, sobretot entre els directius."

De la monitorització diària que ha elaborat 3CatInfo se'n desprèn que Renfe és la companyia que ha hagut d'ajustar més els preus: gairebé un 32%, amb un preu mitjà de 67 euros. També era la que els tenia més alts, i, per competir, els ha hagut de posar semblants als de la competència.

La segueix Ouigo , que fa un any ja tenia un preu mitjà de 61 euros i ara l'ha rebaixat fins als 42,8 euros.

I finalment, qui ha tocat menys el preu és la italiana Iryo , una rebaixa del 16,7% que situa el bitllet en 76 euros de mitjana al novembre de l'any passat, a 63,2 euros durant la primera quinzena.

Tot plegat agreuja la situació financera de les operadores de la línia , que arrosseguen pèrdues des de fa anys.

Ouigo, per exemple, tot i reduir els números vermells, va perdre 18,2 milions d'euros l'any passat a Espanya; Iryo, 12 milions d'euros, i l'única que va guanyar diners per primera vegada en sis anys va ser Renfe, amb un resultat positiu de 58,4 milions gràcies, en part, a l'efecte comptable d'uns ingressos extraordinaris.

Històricament, el pont aeri havia estat la via ràpida per viatjar de Barcelona a Madrid i a la inversa, però des de fa una dècada el 85% dels passatgers que utilitzen aquest corredor ho fan a través del transport ferroviari.

Des que la línia va liberalitzar-se, amb l'entrada d'altres companyies al marge de Renfe, l'ús intensiu del corredor ha multiplicat els usuaris, però també els problemes . Això ha transformat en regla el que abans era excepció: la impuntualitat.
sources.headline: El preu de l'alta velocitat Barcelona-Madrid cau un 28% per la desconfiança dels usuaris
